title: Thinking of cutting the cord with T-Mobile's new streaming service TVision? What you need to know
summary: T-Mobile has launched its new streaming service, TVision, offering cord-cutting options starting at $10 monthly for 30 networks. The service is initially available to T-Mobile postpaid customers, with wider access planned for Sprint subscribers later in the month and other customers next year. TVision provides various packages, including live news and sports, and allows users to add premium channels, though the total cost can rise with additional services.

title: UPS leases 75,000-square-foot Halfmoon warehouse
summary: UPS has leased a 75,000-square-foot former Cardinal Health distribution center in Halfmoon, Saratoga County. This new facility has the potential to employ 125 people and handle a significant volume of daily deliveries, including 140 vans and 20 tractor trailers.

title: Mukesh Ambani versus Jeff Bezos: A fight or a waiting game?
summary: The article details the struggle between Mukesh Ambani and Jeff Bezos for dominance in the Indian consumer market. This centers around Amazon's attempt to block Reliance Industries' $3.4 billion acquisition of Future Group assets, stemming from a previous agreement where Amazon had rights to acquire shares in Future Retail and a non-compete clause with Reliance. The dispute highlights potential issues for foreign investors in India and questions whether Amazon prefers rivalry or a sweeter deal with Ambani.

title: AWS Takes Aim At Oracle By Hiring New Americas Sales Leader
summary: Amazon Web Services (AWS) has hired Rich Geraffo, a former senior vice president at Oracle, to lead its Americas sales organization. This move is seen by partners as a direct challenge to Oracle, aiming to target its database market share and enterprise accounts. Geraffo's extensive experience with Oracle and other enterprise IT companies is expected to bolster AWS's efforts to migrate Fortune 500 companies to its cloud-native services.

title: Homeware Market Forecast, Trend Analysis & Competition Tracking – Global Market insights 2020 to 2024 | Technavio
summary: The global homeware market is projected to grow by USD 79.29 billion between 2020 and 2024, with a CAGR of over 3%. This growth is primarily driven by innovation, portfolio extension, and an increase in the availability of private-label brands. Technavio's report provides market sizing, forecasts, trend analysis, and vendor analysis, including the impact of COVID-19.

title: Walmart drops plans to use robots for tracking inventory
summary: Walmart Inc. has announced it is discontinuing its 5-year partnership with Bossa Nova Robotics, ending plans to use roving robots for inventory tracking in its stores. The retail giant stated it would instead focus on its own technologies and employees to manage inventory, having observed that human workers packaging online orders are already identifying inventory issues. This shift comes after Walmart had initially rolled out shelf-scanning robots in 2017 to improve efficiency and compete with e-commerce rivals.

title: Matson Profit Soars on Goods Shipped From China
summary: Matson Inc. nearly doubled its third-quarter profit to $70.9 million, a 96% increase from the previous year, by capitalizing on expanded shipping services from China to the U.S. mainland. The surge was driven by strong demand for personal protective equipment, home improvement supplies, and e-commerce goods during the pandemic. Matson's CEO expects these trends to continue, leading the company to invest in making its expanded China service permanent.

title: Crushed by virus, 2 mall operators, including operator of Brookfield Square, file for bankruptcy
summary: Two mall operators, CBL & Associates Properties Inc. (operator of Brookfield Square) and Pennsylvania Real Estate Investment Trust, have filed for bankruptcy reorganization due to the COVID-19 pandemic's impact on retail. The pandemic has accelerated the pre-existing trend of declining mall traffic as shoppers shift online, leading to store closures and financial strain on mall tenants. Despite the bankruptcies, both companies plan to keep their malls open, but face challenges from rising coronavirus cases and the crucial holiday shopping season.

title: Matson offers inside glimpse of trans-Pacific pandemonium
summary: Matson CEO Matt Cox described the trans-Pacific shipping market as experiencing "pandemonium," with demand far exceeding capacity and ongoing congestion. The surge is driven by holiday cargo, significant inventory restocking following pandemic depletion, and a dramatic shift to e-commerce, which prioritizes expedited transit. This intense demand has led to nearly double Matson's Q3 2020 profits and a 48% year-to-date stock increase for Matson (NYSE: MATX).

title: An ETF Prepared for More than Black Friday
summary: The article highlights the ProShares Online Retail ETF (ONLN) as a top-rated investment, well-positioned to benefit from the ongoing shift to e-commerce, especially during the holiday season. CFRA has a positive outlook on ONLN due to its strong performance record, appealing holdings like Amazon (AMZN) and eBay (EBAY), and ability to capture growth in online shopping trends amplified by the pandemic. The ETF's significant inflows and strong positions in key e-commerce players are noted as favorable indicators for future outperformance.

title: How Bacardi Served Up a New Digital Experience for Consumers
summary: Bacardi partnered with EPAM to enhance its digital footprint and consumer experience, especially in response to increased at-home consumption during the COVID outbreak. EPAM streamlined Bacardi's digital environment by implementing a new platform, automating deployments for 16x greater capacity, and reducing infrastructure costs by 42%. This transformation allowed Bacardi to reinvest in user experience, maintain brand individuality across 150+ websites, and improve consumer engagement through integrated shopping links and a new CRM system.

title: Pushing for US & Middle East to eat organic, Saudi prince joins Back To The Roots round
summary: Prince Khaled bin Alwaleed bin Talal Al Saud's investment firm, KBW Ventures, has joined a funding round for organic gardening company Back to the Roots. The company, co-led by agrifoodtech specialists S2G Ventures and Acre Venture Partners, sells home organic growkits and seeds, with a focus on US-grown retail seed packets. Prince Khaled, a prominent vegan investor, sees significant market potential for organic produce in the Gulf countries and actively supports companies that positively impact the food chain and offer healthy options.

title: SL Green Sells 410 Tenth Avenue for $953M
summary: SL Green Realty Corp. has announced the sale of its Amazon-anchored 410 Tenth Avenue building for $952.5 million, marking the largest office building sale in the U.S. since the pandemic began. The buyer is reportedly The 601W Companies, led by Mark Karasick and Victor Gerstein. SL Green will retain a 5 percent stake in the property and use the proceeds to reduce debt and potentially repurchase shares.

title: Interesting: In four years Sony quadrupled it’s value while Canon lost more than a third of it’s value
summary: The article highlights a significant divergence in market capitalization between Sony and Canon over four years. Sony quadrupled its value from $27 billion to $105 billion, while Canon's value decreased from $32 billion to $19 billion. This trend is further supported by Sony's dominant 49% share in the CMOS sensor market compared to Canon's negligible presence, suggesting financial troubles for Canon that could impact its camera business.

title: Comcast, Walmart in talks to develop and distribute smart TVs
summary: Comcast and Walmart are reportedly in discussions to develop and distribute smart TVs. This partnership aims to position Comcast as a major streaming hub, with Walmart promoting TVs running Comcast software and sharing in recurring revenue. The move would put them in direct competition with established tech giants like Apple, Amazon, and Roku in the smart TV market.

title: Amazon and Williams-Sonoma settle legal battle over IP
summary: Amazon and Williams-Sonoma have settled a 2018 lawsuit where Williams-Sonoma accused Amazon of counterfeiting its trade name and trademarks, and infringing on them by selling "knockoffs" under Amazon's Rivet brand. The details of the settlement were not disclosed and the judge dismissed the case. This settlement highlights Amazon's ongoing challenges with brands regarding counterfeits and its relationships with sellers on its platform.

title: Vimeo Raises $150 Million of Equity
summary: Vimeo, an IAC company, announced it has raised $150 million in equity funding from Thrive Capital and GIC, valuing the company at $2.75 billion. This investment follows a period of significant growth for Vimeo, driven by demand from business and corporate customers, and will be used to fund further investments in R&D, sales, and international expansion. The professional video platform has scaled to over 200 million users globally and reported profitability and 44% year-over-year revenue growth in the third quarter.

title: SL Green Puts Amazon-Anchored 410 Tenth Under Contract for Nearly $1B
summary: SL Green Realty Corp. has agreed to sell its Amazon-anchored property at 410 Tenth Avenue for $952.5 million, reportedly to 601W Cos. This transaction, if finalized, would be the largest U.S. commercial real estate deal since March. Although initially intended as a long-term investment, the sale will allow SL Green to realize significant profits, reduce debt, and generate funds for share repurchases.

title: Amazon, Williams-Sonoma, reach settlement in legal fight over West Elm IP
summary: Amazon and Williams-Sonoma have settled their legal dispute over West Elm intellectual property. Williams-Sonoma had sued Amazon in 2018, alleging that Amazon's "Rivet" furniture line copied its West Elm products. Details of the confidential settlement were not disclosed.

title: PepsiCo introduces direct-to-consumer e-commerce sites
summary: PepsiCo has launched two direct-to-consumer e-commerce platforms, PantryShop.com and Snacks.com, in response to increased online shopping due to the coronavirus pandemic. PantryShop.com offers bundled product collections, while Snacks.com allows consumers to curate snack packages from Frito-Lay brands. This initiative aims to provide consumers with easy and fast access to their favorite PepsiCo products delivered directly to their homes.

title: Mattel CEO: Barbie, Hot Wheels, 'are resonating' with consumers during pandemic
summary: Mattel CEO Ynon Kreiz reports that the toy company's turnaround is gaining momentum, with strong third-quarter sales driven by brands like Barbie and Hot Wheels. The company saw a 10% year-over-year increase in net sales to $1.6 billion and a 131% surge in adjusted operating profits. Kreiz also highlighted 10 film projects and several TV shows in development for 2021, aiming to further boost toy sales and leverage his content creation background.

title: FAANG stands for five very successful tech companies that can move the stock market — here's what to know about investing in them
summary: The article defines FAANG as an acronym representing Facebook, Amazon, Apple, Netflix, and Google, five influential tech companies that significantly impact the stock market. It details their historical performance, their combined market capitalization, and how investors can invest in them, either individually or through various tech and index funds. The piece emphasizes their role as modern-day blue-chip stocks and their substantial impact on the S&P 500 and the broader US economy.

title: Nest Wifi vs. Ubiquiti AmpliFi HD: Which should you buy?
summary: This article compares Google's Nest Wifi and Ubiquiti AmpliFi HD mesh Wi-Fi systems, detailing their strengths, weaknesses, and key differences. While Nest Wifi offers Google Assistant integration and WPA3 support, AmpliFi HD excels in coverage, QoS options, wired backhaul, and a free VPN solution. The article concludes that AmpliFi HD is generally the superior product due to its broader feature set and performance advantages.

title: Grocers look to online subscriptions to lock in digital demand
summary: Grocery retailers like Kroger, Ahold Delhaize, and Albertsons are increasingly offering online subscription programs for delivery or pickup to capitalize on the shift to digital shopping and build customer loyalty. These programs serve as a defensive measure against competitors like Amazon Prime and Walmart+, aiming to retain existing customers and attract new ones. Experts suggest that grocers need to offer additional perks beyond just delivery fee waivers to make these subscriptions truly valuable and differentiate themselves from third-party services like Instacart.

title: Prisma Access: SASE Architected for Unprecedented Security and Scale
summary: Palo Alto Networks' Prisma Access service, combined with CloudGenix SD-WAN, offers a comprehensive SASE platform designed for unprecedented security and scale. Leveraging cloud-native architecture on AWS and Google Cloud, it provides extensive global coverage and ultra-fast security processing, proven by its ability to support massive increases in remote workers during the COVID-19 pandemic. The service has demonstrated rapid scalability, enabling major organizations like PwC, Schlumberger, and Flex to transition significant portions of their workforce to remote operations without disruption.

title: Roku vs. Fire TV: Which cheap smart TV is better?
summary: This article compares Roku and Amazon Fire TV operating systems for smart TVs, evaluating them across navigation, app selection, search, voice recognition, privacy, and smart home integration. It concludes that Roku provides a better overall user experience due to its simpler interface, easier app management, and greater independence, despite Amazon Fire TV's stronger smart home capabilities via Alexa.

title: Sprouts Farmers Market prepares to open next Orlando store
summary: Sprouts Farmers Market is set to open its third location in metro Orlando on November 18 at 603 Turkey Lake Road. This new store will join its existing Central Florida branches in Oviedo and Winter Park. The Phoenix-based grocer continues its expansion in the region.

title: Zoom and other ‘stay-at-home’ stocks got crushed on the positive vaccine news
summary: Shares of "stay-at-home" stocks like Zoom, Amazon, and Netflix dropped significantly after positive news regarding a COVID-19 vaccine from Pfizer and BioNTech. Investors rotated out of these pandemic-benefiting companies and into those expected to gain from an economic reopening, such as banks and cruise lines.

title: Amazon expands in Brazil, riding e-commerce boom set off by COVID-19 distancing
summary: Amazon has opened three new logistics centers in Brazil, bringing its total to eight, to capitalize on the e-commerce surge driven by the COVID-19 pandemic. This expansion, adding 75,000 square meters of distribution space and 1,500 direct jobs, will significantly increase delivery speed for Amazon Prime customers in the country. Brazil is experiencing rapid growth in Amazon Prime subscriptions and a broader shift to digital sales, with other e-commerce companies also reporting significant revenue increases.

title: Descartes acquires e-commerce shipment tracking firm for $19 million
summary: Descartes Systems Group has acquired ShipTrack, an e-commerce shipment tracking firm, for $19 million, with the potential for the deal to rise to $38 million based on performance targets. This acquisition aims to strengthen Descartes' e-commerce final-mile capabilities and integrate ShipTrack's cloud-based mobile resource management and shipment tracking solutions into Descartes' Global Logistics Network. The move reflects Descartes' strategy to invest in e-commerce capabilities amidst a permanent shift towards online purchasing.

title: Check Point CloudGuard integrates with AWS Gateway Load Balancer at Launch
summary: Check Point CloudGuard has integrated with the newly launched AWS Gateway Load Balancer (GWLB) to enhance cloud security for AWS customers. This integration allows for simplified deployment, scaling, and management of virtual network appliances like CloudGuard security gateways within AWS, ensuring high availability and advanced threat prevention. The article explains how GWLB works with CloudGuard to provide transparent traffic inspection, reduced network complexity, and consistent security policies across hybrid cloud environments.

title: Booking.com, Expedia Group, Hotels.com customers in suspected data breach
summary: Customers who booked hotels using platforms like Hotels.com, Booking.com, and Expedia in the past seven years are at risk due to a suspected data breach. Prestige Software, a company servicing these platforms, reportedly exposed millions of guests' data, including names, credit card details, and ID numbers, through a misconfigured Amazon Web Services S3 bucket. A security team discovered the breach, which exposed highly sensitive information from as far back as 2013, warning of significant implications for privacy and financial well-being due to potential fraud and online attacks.

title: 10 Websites to Make $100 per Day Working From Home (Without Investment!)
summary: This article lists ten websites that can help individuals earn $100 per day working from home without an upfront investment. It covers various online opportunities like freelancing, affiliate marketing, content creation, and online tutoring, detailing how each platform works and payment methods. The goal is to provide readers with diverse options to supplement their income or make a full-time living online.

title: Bienvenue Cloudflare France! Why I’m helping Cloudflare grow in France
summary: Boris Lecoeur announces his new role as Head of France for Cloudflare, marking the company's fourth office in the EMEA region. He outlines his reasons for joining, highlighting Cloudflare's impressive growth, extensive global network, rapid innovation, and strong company culture. Lecoeur plans to expand Cloudflare's presence and support existing and new customers, partners, and employees in France, a country with a vibrant tech ecosystem.

title: Buy now! COVID-19 sparks Southeast Asian e-commerce boom
summary: The COVID-19 pandemic has significantly accelerated e-commerce growth in Southeast Asia, with spending expected to triple to over $300 billion by 2025. While online travel and transport were hit, overall digital adoption surged, bringing 40 million new internet users online in the region in 2020. Indonesia's digital economy is also projected to nearly triple despite the wider economic downturn.

title: Crazy sale! China’s Singles’ Day bags record shopping revenues
summary: Alibaba's Singles' Day shopping festival achieved record sales of over $56 billion by Wednesday morning, surpassing 2019 figures, despite recent market valuation losses for Alibaba following the Ant Group's suspended listing. The event benefited from China's economic rebound post-COVID-19 and increased consumer reliance on e-commerce, with luxury brands seeing a boon due to travel restrictions. Other platforms like JD.com also reported significant sales.

title: Amdocs bolsters AWS relationship, reports record sales, sells unit
summary: Amdocs reported record quarterly revenues of $1.053 billion, strengthening its position in the software and cloud-oriented telecoms industry. The company also expanded its strategic alliance with Amazon Web Services, making AWS its preferred cloud provider, and agreed to sell its non-strategic OpenMarket unit for $300 million. This financial performance and strategic moves demonstrate Amdocs's growth trajectory and adaptability in a changing market.

title: Size-Inclusive Fashion Line From Revered Designer Jason Wu To Launch At QVC®
summary: QVC is launching a size-inclusive fashion line called "J Jason Wu," designed by the acclaimed fashion designer Jason Wu. The collection will be available in sizes 5X to XXS (32-0) and will feature classic American sportswear essentials with a couture sensibility. This collaboration further extends QVC's commitment to offering fashion that celebrates all body types at the same price points, regardless of size.

title: FedEx Survey: Record Number of Online Shoppers and Shipments Projected This Holiday Season
summary: A FedEx survey projects a record number of online shoppers and shipments this holiday season, with 81% of Canadians planning to shop online and 35% of first-time online holiday shoppers joining them. The survey also revealed a rise in reported package theft, prompting FedEx to urge early shopping and highlight tools like FedEx Delivery Manager to help secure deliveries. FedEx Express Canada has expanded operations and hired additional staff to manage the anticipated peak in shipping volumes.

title: Best Buy adds Lovesac products to online assortment
summary: Best Buy has expanded its partnership with furniture brand Lovesac by selling its products online, allowing Lovesac to reach a broader customer base. This move capitalizes on the increased consumer spending in home goods and e-commerce during the pandemic, benefiting both companies as Best Buy also saw a rise in sales due to investments in tech for remote work and learning. The collaboration aims to position Best Buy as a "one-stop shop" for consumers, aligning with the booming sales of gaming accessories and other electronics during the holiday season.

title: The Snowflake Story
summary: Snowflake Inc., founded in 2012, is a cloud-based data-warehousing company that came out of stealth mode in 2014. The company offers a data warehouse-as-a-service, running on major cloud platforms and enabling data storage and analytics for corporate users. Snowflake had a historic IPO on September 16, 2020, with shares more than doubling in value, leading to a $70.4 billion market valuation on its first day of trading.

title: Q&A: XPO Logistics talks COVID response, supply chain hurdles
summary: Drew Wilkerson, president of North American transportation at XPO Logistics, discusses the company's response to the COVID-19 pandemic, focusing on employee safety, maintaining operations, and helping customers adapt. He highlights how XPO reconfigured its operations, implemented extensive safety measures, and utilized its XPO Connect platform to manage shifting freight demands and support drivers and customers during the unprecedented events of 2020. Wilkerson also shares insights into future trends, especially the continued growth of e-commerce and contactless deliveries.

title: FedEx in Partnership to Use Facilities as Cloud Service Hubs
summary: Dell Technologies Inc., FedEx Corp., and Switch Inc. are collaborating to build a U.S. network of data centers, offering businesses a hybrid cloud alternative. These hubs, leveraging Dell hardware and FedEx facilities, aim to provide faster computing speeds by being closer to clients than large centralized public cloud providers. This initiative allows businesses to host private clouds and pay based on usage, marking Dell's strategic move into the hybrid-cloud market.

title: Former Amazon.com employee sues over COVID worker safety issues
summary: A former Amazon.com employee, Christian Smalls, has sued the retailer, alleging discrimination and failure to protect predominantly minority workers at its New York City facility from COVID-19. Smalls claims Amazon fired him for being a "weak spokesman" as a Black man and subjected minority employees to inferior working conditions. The lawsuit seeks unspecified damages for Black and Hispanic workers, while Amazon asserts Smalls was fired for violating quarantine protocols.

title: Pinduoduo Stock Jumps As Third-Quarter Results Top Estimates
summary: Pinduoduo (PDD) reported third-quarter results that significantly exceeded Wall Street expectations, leading to a substantial jump in its stock price. The China-based e-commerce company posted adjusted earnings of 5 cents per share on revenue of $2.1 billion, far surpassing analysts' estimates of a 17-cent loss and $1.86 billion in revenue. Following the announcement, PDD stock soared by 20.4%, closing at 134.21.

title: Amazon shifts some voice assistant, face recognition computing to its own chips
summary: Amazon is transitioning some of the computing for its Alexa voice assistant and Rekognition facial recognition service to its custom-designed "Inferentia" chips. This strategic move aims to improve speed and reduce costs by moving away from third-party chip providers like Nvidia. The company reports a 25% improvement in latency and 30% lower costs for Alexa's text-to-speech tasks with the new chips.

title: Amazon Announces New, State-of-the-Art Fulfillment Center to be Built in Mississippi
summary: Amazon is set to build a new 700,000 square-foot robotics fulfillment center in Madison County, Mississippi, creating over 1,000 new full-time jobs. This facility will be Amazon's first in Mississippi to feature innovative robotics technology and will enhance the company's ability to serve customers in the region. The move is expected to bring significant economic benefits and employment opportunities to Madison County, with Amazon offering industry-leading pay and comprehensive benefits.

title: 8x8 delivers high-quality service with OCI flexible shapes and global regions
summary: 8x8, a leading unified communications provider, enhanced its service quality and cost-performance by migrating its global meeting services and core infrastructure from AWS and legacy data centers to Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI). The move resulted in significant cost reductions, improved performance, and better support. 8x8 leveraged OCI's flexible shapes, global regions, and services like OCI Logging Analytics and OCI Kubernetes Engine to achieve greater efficiency, scalability, and real-time visibility into its operations.

title: UPS, FedEx Face Stress Test From Amazon’s ‘Christmas Creep’
summary: UPS and FedEx are facing their biggest stress test yet due to the "Christmas Creep" phenomenon, where holiday shopping is starting earlier and straining already capacity-limited shipping networks. This year's early promotions, including Amazon's Prime Day, are pushing billions in sales and forcing carriers to ramp up hiring and capacity earlier than ever. The demand surge, exacerbated by the pandemic, has led to increased profits and stock performance for both companies, but also raises concerns about potential capacity shortages.

title: How Walmart, Kroger Plan to Become Advertising Giants
summary: Walmart and Kroger are looking to become major players in online advertising, capitalizing on the pandemic-driven surge in e-commerce. These retail titans aim to leverage increased online traffic and consumer data to boost long-term profits through their advertising platforms. The accelerated shift to e-commerce has provided a significant opportunity for these well-positioned retailers.

title: Why Google, Amazon, and Nvidia are all building AI notetakers for doctors
summary: Google, Amazon, and Nvidia are developing AI-powered notetaking tools for doctors to address the time-consuming and often inaccurate process of medical transcription. These tools aim to improve the efficiency and accuracy of recording patient interactions and medical records, moving beyond existing methods that doctors find cumbersome or overly generalized. While some solutions are already available, tech giants are focusing on delivering more precise and sophisticated AI to streamline healthcare documentation.

title: Sony PS5 sold out online as pandemic chills real-world retailing
summary: Sony's PlayStation 5 console launched to high demand but was sold out online in major markets due to the company's decision to make sales online-only to encourage social distancing during the pandemic. This led to consoles being resold for significantly higher prices on platforms like Mercari. Consumers who pre-ordered, like New York resident Anil Rivera, collected their consoles at stores.

title: How to check if you have latest motherboard BIOS for AMD Ryzen 5000 CPUs
summary: This article provides a guide on how to check and update the motherboard BIOS to support AMD Ryzen 5000 series CPUs. It includes comprehensive lists of compatible X570, B550, and A520 motherboards from various manufacturers like ASRock, ASUS, GIGABYTE, and MSI, along with their minimum required BIOS versions. The guide details both automatic and manual BIOS update methods and recommends specific AMD Ryzen 5900X CPU and ASUS TUF Gaming B550M-Plus motherboard.

title: Walmart sells majority stake in Japanese Seiyu supermarket
summary: Walmart is selling 85% of its Japanese supermarket subsidiary, Seiyu, for ¥172.5 billion ($1.6 billion). Global investment firm KKR & Co. will acquire a 65% stake, while Japanese online retailer Rakuten will take a 20% stake, with Walmart retaining the remaining 15%. This move aims to strengthen Seiyu in the evolving digital retail landscape by leveraging KKR and Rakuten's e-commerce and digital marketing expertise.

title: JPMorgan Chase to expand to Mississippi, build branches in Jackson
summary: JPMorgan Chase & Co. announced plans to open its first Mississippi branch in Jackson's Highland Village Shopping Center by April 2021, creating eight to 10 new jobs with entry-level positions starting at $15 an hour plus full benefits. This initial branch is part of a larger strategy to expand into the Jackson metro area, driven by the region's recent economic growth and the bank's existing client base in Mississippi.

title: How 6 chains expanded pickup during the pandemic
summary: The COVID-19 pandemic accelerated the adoption of grocery pickup services, with several major chains rapidly expanding their offerings. Companies like Kroger, Walmart, Albertsons, Target, Ahold Delhaize, and Whole Foods leveraged existing infrastructures or quickly implemented new strategies to meet soaring consumer demand for convenient, contactless shopping. These expansions included increasing store availability, adding more pickup slots and parking spaces, integrating fresh and frozen groceries, waiving fees, and exploring technological advancements for efficiency.

title: 115 Amazon lobbyists. 1 works on climate
summary: Despite Amazon's public stance on climate action and its "Climate Pledge," an analysis reveals that only one out of its 115 lobbyists is focused on environmental issues. This raises questions about the company's commitment, with critics suggesting it may be "greenwashing." Other tech giants like Facebook also show similar discrepancies, while Microsoft, Apple, and Google appear to align their lobbying efforts more closely with their climate concerns.

title: Barbie Extra: The five dolls in Mattel's latest Barbie line each come with a pet
summary: Mattel has released a new "Barbie Extra" line featuring five unique dolls, each accompanied by a pet. The dolls are designed with diverse hairstyles, clothing, and accessories, reflecting flamboyant styles, and are available at retailers like Target, Walmart, and Amazon for $24.99 each.

title: Walmart sells majority stake in Seiyu, nearly exiting Japan
summary: Walmart is selling a majority stake in its Japanese supermarket chain Seiyu to investment firm KKR and e-commerce company Rakuten for over $1 billion. This move effectively nearly exits Walmart from the Japanese market, following years of struggling to compete and recent divestitures in other international markets. Walmart will retain a 15% stake in Seiyu, while KKR will acquire 65% and Rakuten 20%.

title: 11st could start carrying Amazon products from next year
summary: SK Telecom announced a partnership with Amazon that will allow Korean consumers to purchase Amazon products directly through the 11st website, potentially starting next year. Amazon has also secured pre-emptive rights to acquire stock in 11st after it goes public, with the exact number of shares dependent on 11st's business performance. This collaboration is expected to accelerate 11st's goal of becoming a global retail and logistics platform and could create synergies with SK Telecom's other businesses, such as its subscription and OTT services.

title: Amazon opens online pharmacy, disrupting another industry
summary: Amazon has launched an online pharmacy service, allowing customers to order prescriptions for home delivery. This move significantly impacted the pharmaceutical sector, causing stock drops for CVS Health Corp., Walgreens, and Rite Aid, as analysts predict a shift in prescription fulfillment from traditional retail channels to Amazon. The company's entry into health care, following its 2018 acquisition of PillPack, is seen as a major disruption, potentially leading to its evolution into a pharmacy benefit manager.

title: Amazon Pharmacy is live: Shoppers can now order prescriptions directly through the tech giant
summary: Amazon has launched Amazon Pharmacy, allowing customers to order prescription medications online, including discounts for Prime members who pay without insurance. This move places Amazon in direct competition with major pharmacy chains like CVS and Walgreens and has already impacted their stock prices. Amazon aims to leverage its digital presence and logistics to address inefficiencies in the pharmaceutical industry and increase transparency in drug pricing.

title: Information Leakage in AWS Resource-Based Policy APIs
summary: Unit 42 researchers identified that 22 AWS APIs across 16 services can be abused to leak AWS IAM users and roles in arbitrary accounts. This vulnerability stems from AWS's proactive validation of resource-based policies, which inadvertently reveals identity existence through error messages. The technique is stealthy, as logs only appear in the attacker's account, making detection and prevention difficult for targeted accounts.

title: 1,100 homes greenlit on Columbus' western edge
summary: Harmony Development and Pulte Homes have received approval for two new housing developments, Sugar Farms and Renner South, on Columbus' western edge. These projects collectively greenlight 1,098 new homes and are located along Alton Darby Creek Road. The build-out for these developments is expected to take between eight to ten years.

title: Amazon Echo Studio review: best sounding Echo by far assails Sonos One with hi-def and 3D audio
summary: The Amazon Echo Studio is reviewed as the best-sounding Echo speaker to date, offering support for CD-quality, hi-res, and 3D audio at a competitive price. While it provides a powerful sound and deep bass, especially for electronic music and hip-hop, it lacks the refinement and aesthetic appeal of its main rival, the Sonos One. The Studio is particularly valuable for Amazon Music HD subscribers, though 3D audio content is currently limited.

title: Fall Shopping Events Pouring on the Gains for EBIZ ETFs
summary: The Global X E-commerce ETF (NasdaqGM: EBIZ) is performing well, driven by the booming e-commerce economy highlighted by events like Amazon's Prime Day and Alibaba's Singles Day. The article discusses how the pandemic has accelerated online retail growth, presenting significant opportunities for investors in companies related to e-commerce platforms, software, and online sales. U.S. online sales are projected to reach $795 billion in 2020, demonstrating substantial growth and long-term upside for EBIZ.

title: Amazon expands into healthcare with online pharmacy
summary: Amazon has launched Amazon Pharmacy, a new service allowing customers to order prescription medications online, intensifying its competition with pharmacy giants like CVS and Walgreens. This expansion, building on its 2018 acquisition of PillPack, offers discounts to Prime members and aims to bring transparency and convenience to the healthcare industry. The announcement caused significant drops in the stock prices of major drugstore chains and drug distributors.

title: ICE Seeks Large New Cloud Contract Involving Microsoft, Amazon
summary: U.S. Immigrations and Customs Enforcement (ICE) is planning significant new expenditures on cloud computing with Microsoft Corp. and Amazon.com Inc.'s Amazon Web Services (AWS). This deal, expected in early 2021, could reignite internal tensions within these companies, where employees have previously objected to collaborations with agencies involved in family separations and immigrant raids. ICE is seeking a third-party contractor to manage and expand its existing systems in AWS and Microsoft Azure environments.

title: Amazon launches online pharmacy in new contest with drug retail
summary: Amazon.com Inc launched an online pharmacy for delivering prescription medications in the United States, intensifying competition with established drug retailers like Walgreens, CVS Health, and Walmart. The new Amazon Pharmacy allows customers to compare prices, including discounted rates for Prime members, and builds on Amazon's 2018 acquisition of PillPack. This move caused shares of traditional drug retail chains and wholesalers to fall, while Amazon's shares rose.

title: Introducing Amazon Pharmacy: Prescription Medications Delivered
summary: Amazon.com, Inc. announced the launch of Amazon Pharmacy, allowing customers to purchase prescription medications online and access prescription savings. Amazon Prime members benefit from free two-day delivery on pharmacy orders and significant discounts on medications. This new offering aims to provide convenient and affordable access to prescription drugs, building on Amazon's existing PillPack service for chronic conditions.

title: A COVID Shadow Gives Black Friday Retail New Meaning
summary: This article discusses the unique challenges and opportunities for retail during Black Friday 2020 due to the COVID-19 pandemic. It suggests that while the virus casts a shadow, there's potential for revenue boosts, particularly highlighted by the Direxion Daily Retail Bull 3X ETF (RETL B+). The article also touches upon the "K-shaped" recovery and the resilience of U.S. consumers, noting strong spending in certain sectors like home goods.

title: Walmart’s Sales Gains Slow as Pandemic Drags On
summary: Walmart's quarterly sales growth slowed compared to earlier in the pandemic, despite continued strong sales of food and cleaning supplies and early holiday promotions. While comparable U.S. sales rose 6.4%, e-commerce sales significantly boosted these gains, jumping 79% and contributing substantially to the latest quarter's performance. The retailer experienced a sharp drop in in-store visits even as online sales soared.

title: ‘Do the hard things first’: What Capital One prioritized in its cloud migration
summary: Capital One's VP of Technology, Allison Perkel, advises companies undergoing cloud migration to tackle the most challenging aspects first. For Capital One, this meant prioritizing robust cybersecurity controls, drawing lessons from software development principles. The company's eight-year cloud journey to AWS, which involved closing its final data center, persevered despite a significant data breach in 2019, reinforcing the strategic importance of cloud adoption.

title: Tesla Added to the S&P 500
summary: S&P Dow Jones Indices announced that Tesla would be added to the S&P 500 prior to the market open on Monday, December 21, 2020. This article discusses the S&P 500's methodology, the significance of Tesla's inclusion, and its potential impact on the market, noting that Tesla's float market capitalization of USD 304 billion would make it the largest S&P 500 addition ever. The addition is expected to increase the weight of the Consumer Discretionary sector in the index and potentially reduce the sector's sensitivity to Amazon.

title: WWE SuperCard Season 7 Now Available
summary: 2K Games has released Season 7 of WWE SuperCard, introducing new features, card tiers, and gameplay mechanics. The update includes Styles & Techniques, Super Moves, three new card tiers (Bio-Mechanical, Behemoth, Swarm), and an art refresh. Players can also earn rewards through dynamic Collections and participate in a new WarGames event.

title: GoodRx Shares Plunge After Amazon Announces Online Pharmacy
summary: GoodRx Holdings Inc. shares plunged nearly 28% after Amazon.com Inc. announced its entrance into the online pharmacy market, including a service offering steep prescription drug discounts to Prime customers. This move led to an immediate downgrade of GoodRx stock by a JPMorgan Chase analyst and raised concerns about GoodRx's operating margins due to potential price competition. Amazon's offering, which includes online purchasing for home delivery and discounts that could rival GoodRx's, positions it as a significant competitor in the prescription drug market.

title: Add Gurnee Mills to the growing list of financially troubled shopping malls in the greater Milwaukee area
summary: Gurnee Mills, a large regional shopping destination in Illinois, has been added to the list of financially troubled malls in the greater Milwaukee area after its $255.9 million loan became delinquent and was transferred to "special servicing." This issue, exacerbated by the COVID-19 pandemic, reflects a broader trend of declining mall occupancy rates and financial distress affecting traditional retail properties. Simon Property Group Inc. also plans to transfer ownership of Southridge Mall to its lender, highlighting the challenges faced by indoor shopping malls.

title: Mizuho to cut Singapore office space on work-from-home success
summary: Mizuho Financial Group is planning to reduce its office space in Singapore by about 16% at Asia Square Tower 2, following similar moves in New York and London. The Japanese bank is adapting its workspace strategy after the pandemic proved employees remained productive while working from home, leading to lower office occupancy rates even after social distancing rules were relaxed. While cost reduction isn't the primary goal, Mizuho also intends to redesign its Singapore office for a more open, communal environment suitable for a younger workforce, incorporating safe management measures.

title: Why climate change is getting the attention of world's wealthy investors
summary: Wealthy investors are increasingly focusing on climate change as a fundamental investment theme, driven by significant economic opportunities rather than political beliefs. Billionaires like Jeff Bezos and Elon Musk are leading the way, but this trend is also widespread among ultra-wealthy investors who see renewables becoming cheaper and creating vast capital investment opportunities. Despite concerns about short-term political uncertainties or the intermittency of renewable energy, experts believe the investment case for green technologies and addressing climate risk in portfolios remains strong, with potential for comparable performance to traditional investments.

title: Target releases Black Friday ad with deals on electronics, toys, more starting Sunday. What's different amid COVID?
summary: Target has released its fourth and final Black Friday ad for 2020, with deals starting Sunday and running through November 28th. Amid the coronavirus pandemic, Target, like other retailers, is spreading out deals over several weeks to reduce crowds, offering "Black Friday Now" sales and extending its Price Match Guarantee through December 24th. The retailer will also remain closed on Thanksgiving Day, a change from previous years.

title: Amazon delays Black Friday in France amid outcry from small biz
summary: Amazon and other major retailers in France have agreed to postpone Black Friday from November 27 to December 4. This decision was made following an outcry from smaller retailers who sought to reopen their physical stores before the promotional event. The postponement aims to allow non-essential stores, which have been closed since October 30 due to COVID-19 restrictions, an opportunity to resume operations.

title: CVS Health and Walgreens Can Fend Off the Amazon Pharmacy Threat
summary: Amazon's launch of Amazon Pharmacy, offering free two-day prescription delivery and discounts, caused a significant drop in stock prices for major pharmacy chains like CVS Health and Walgreens. Despite the immediate market reaction, the article suggests that these established pharmacies are well-positioned to counter the threat. This indicates that while the competition is new, incumbents have strategies to retain their market share.

title: The 1stdibs Holiday Sale Kicks Off, a Pig Couch Causes a Mystery, and More News This Week
summary: This article provides a weekly roundup of news in the design world, covering various topics from sales and auctions to product launches and industry events. Key highlights include 1stDibs's holiday sale, an auction of a segment of the Eiffel Tower's staircase, and West Elm's new partnership with Muji. The report also touches on intriguing news such as the "pig couch" mystery and MoMA's new institute dedicated to the built and natural environment.

title: Now that's multicloud: CIA awards multibillion-dollar contract to AWS, Microsoft, Google, Oracle and IBM
summary: The CIA has awarded its Commercial Cloud Enterprise (C2E) contract to Amazon Web Services, Microsoft, Google, Oracle, and IBM, marking a significant shift to a multicloud strategy. This multibillion-dollar contract allows these five major public cloud providers to compete for task orders from the CIA and 16 other intelligence agencies across different security classification levels. This move aims to leverage the unique strengths of various providers for different workloads and enhance competition, contrasting with past single-vendor awards like the Department of Defense's JEDI contract.

title: Plug Power Has Soared This Year. How Walmart, Amazon Also Benefited From the Green-Energy Rally.
summary: Plug Power's stock has surged sixfold in 2020, reaching $25 a share, following a nearly $1 billion stock offering. The company, a pioneer in clean-energy power supplies for forklifts, has seen significant demand from major customers like Walmart and Amazon. This growth highlights the broader green-energy rally from which these large retailers have also benefited.

title: Holiday Bonus Alternatives for Employees
summary: This article explores various alternatives for small businesses to show employee appreciation during the holidays when traditional cash bonuses might not be feasible, especially in economically challenging times like 2020. It highlights creative methods such as enhancing home office setups, organizing virtual events, providing personalized care packages, offering extra time off, distributing quality company swag, and catering holiday meals. The piece emphasizes that recognition through praise and thoughtful gestures can be as impactful as financial rewards.

title: Amazon plans new distribution center near San Antonio airport
summary: Amazon received zoning approval for a new 141,000 square feet "last-mile" distribution center near the San Antonio airport. The facility, located on a 55-acre vacant lot, aims to expedite package delivery to customers in the San Antonio area. City Council approval is still pending for the project.

title: Coca-Cola Is Open to Inorganic Growth in Still Beverages
summary: Coca-Cola is looking towards inorganic growth, specifically acquisitions, to expand its presence in the high-growth still beverages market. This strategy is in response to the continued underperformance of carbonated soft drinks compared to categories like bottled water, ready-to-drink coffee, and energy drinks. The company has already made strategic moves, including the acquisition of Innocent Drinks and a stake in Suja Juice and Monster Beverage.

title: Why Ross Stores Isn’t Keen on E-Commerce Growth
summary: Ross Stores, an off-price retailer, isn't pursuing e-commerce growth due to the low average price of its merchandise ($10), which makes online sales unprofitable after factoring in shipping and return costs. The company's business model relies on small lot sizes, which is difficult to replicate online, even as rivals like Nordstrom Rack, TJX Companies, and Burlington Stores expand their digital presence.

title: Why Rackspace Revenue Growth Has Slowed Down
summary: Rackspace's revenue growth has slowed despite the increasing preference for cloud services due to a change in its strategy, which includes offering bundled computing and support services and potentially higher pricing compared to competitors. The company had considered a merger or buyout in 2014 but ultimately decided against it, opting to appoint a new CEO, Taylor Rhodes, to lead its revised operational strategy.

title: St. Louis shoe company Caleres to shutter 133 Naturalizer stores to focus on ecommerce
summary: St. Louis-based footwear company Caleres announced its plan to close 133 Naturalizer retail locations. This strategic move is aimed at shifting the brand's focus towards e-commerce. Caleres intends to prioritize its online presence for the Naturalizer brand.

title: The Value of Data in a Digital World
summary: This article discusses the increasing value of data in a digital world, contrasting it with the historical valuation of companies based on tangible assets. It explores why data should be considered an asset, despite current accounting rules, and proposes three approaches for data valuation: market-based, cost-based, and cash flow-based, providing examples for each. The article also touches on how data-rich enterprises can seize opportunities and mentions related ETFs that invest in data-centric technologies.

title: Gov. Hogan names College Park quantum computing company one of top state start-ups
summary: Maryland Gov. Larry Hogan recognized IonQ, a College Park quantum computing company, as one of the top 20 start-up companies in the state. IonQ, based in the Discovery District, is developing quantum computers and software, including a system currently working with both Amazon and Microsoft. The university has invested $5.5 million in the company and utilizes its research, contributing to College Park's aim to become a quantum computing hub.

title: Forget FAANG—it’s time to scale MT SAAS
summary: Bessemer Venture Partners introduces "MT SAAS" (Microsoft, Twilio, Salesforce, Amazon, Adobe, Shopify) as the new basket of top public technology companies, succeeding the traditional "FAANG" stocks. This new group represents leaders in cloud computing, identified as the mega-trend of the next decade, and has shown significant outperformance compared to FAANG stocks over recent years. The article details the characteristics and growth trajectories of each MT SAAS company, highlighting their cloud-first strategies and substantial market capitalization gains.

title: Hasbro makes some noise with Peppa Pig
summary: Hasbro is expanding Peppa Pig's presence into the audio streaming market with a new series of 10 audio stories to be released globally on platforms like Amazon Prime, Apple Music, and Spotify. This move follows the success of Peppa Pig's first digital music album, which garnered 24 million streams worldwide. The new audio content will feature stories inspired by popular episodes of the show, joining a growing number of kids' audio offerings.

title: TJX retailers launch ‘Carol for a Cause’ holiday campaign
summary: T.J. Maxx, HomeGoods, and Marshalls have launched their "Carol for a Cause" holiday campaign, encouraging consumers to record and share carols on Instagram Reels. For each post with #CarolForACause, the retailers will donate $10 to Feeding America, up to $1 million, to recreate holiday caroling amidst the COVID-19 pandemic. The campaign features celebrity artists and coincides with HomeGoods' upcoming e-commerce site launch, reflecting Instagram's growing role in commerce.

title: With e-commerce exploding, FedEx Ground opens another Lehigh Valley facility with plans to hire 1,300
summary: FedEx Ground has opened a new 970,000-square-foot regional sortation facility in Upper Macungie Township, Lehigh Valley, intending to hire 1,300 permanent employees. This expansion, supplementing their existing hub, is driven by the explosive growth of e-commerce during the pandemic and aims to enhance package sorting capabilities, processing over 40,000 packages per hour. The company's local workforce in Lehigh Valley is projected to exceed 3,000 once the new facility is fully staffed.

title: Smart City Platform Market May See a Big Move | Cisco Systems, Intel, NEC
summary: The Global Smart City Platform Market was valued at approximately USD 124.7 billion in 2019 and is projected to grow at over 11.2% annually from 2020 to 2027. Key drivers include rising urban populations, the increasing adoption of IoT technology, and digital transformations. Major players like Cisco Systems, IBM, Siemens, Hitachi, Microsoft, Schneider Electric, Huawei, Intel, NEC, and Amazon Web Services are profiled in a new HTF MI report.

title: Amazon is price gouging cleaning products for the second COVID wave
summary: During the second COVID-19 wave, Amazon sellers are price gouging cleaning products from name brands like Clorox, Bounty, and Charmin, while generic alternatives remain relatively more stable. Clorox wipe prices, for instance, have surged over 200% since January, reaching as high as $50 for a pack. This practice is occurring despite earlier efforts by companies like Clorox to address price gouging on the platform.

title: AMC Plus Launches on Roku Channel
summary: AMC Networks announced that its premium streaming service, AMC Plus, is now available on The Roku Channel. The service, priced at $8.99 a month, offers original programming from AMC's cable networks and streaming services, including "The Walking Dead Universe" and "Mad Men." This launch expands AMC Plus's distribution, following recent additions to Prime Video Channels, Apple TV channels, Comcast, Dish, and Sling TV.

title: Should you invest in technology sector funds?
summary: This article discusses the performance and prospects of technology sector funds in India, highlighting their strong returns during the pandemic and the factors influencing their growth. It explores investment options including domestic and international tech funds, the outlook for Indian IT firms, and crucial risks and investment strategies investors should consider, such as staggering investments via SIPs.

title: Everyone's favorite paint-mixing TikTok star just got fired by Sherwin-Williams
summary: Tony Piloseno, a Sherwin-Williams employee known for his viral paint-mixing TikTok channel, was fired by the company despite his efforts to pitch a marketing collaboration. The company accused him of using company time and stealing paint, though Piloseno stated he purchased the paint himself. This incident highlights contrasting approaches by corporations regarding employee innovation, with Sherwin-Williams' decision potentially harming its public image.

title: Omaha’s AMC Oakview Plaza 24 closes permanently
summary: AMC's Oakview Plaza 24 movie theater in Omaha has permanently closed its doors on November 8, after nearly 23 years of operation. The closure is a result of financial strains exacerbated by the COVID-19 pandemic, leading landlords to terminate leases with AMC. This specific theater is one of six nationwide affected by an agreement with landlord EPR Properties, though other AMC locations in the Omaha-Council Bluffs area remain open.

title: Ozon IPO Is First U.S. Listing Of A Russian-Based Firm In 18 Months
summary: Russian e-commerce company Ozon Holdings (OZON) successfully raised $990 million in its initial public offering, marking the first U.S. listing by a Russian-based firm in 18 months. The IPO began trading on Tuesday afternoon. Ozon's listing on U.S. domestic exchanges breaks a dry spell for Russian IPOs since May 2019.

title: Leonard A. Lauder Looks Back on His Life in Business
summary: Leonard A. Lauder's memoir, "The Company I Keep: My Life in Beauty," quickly became a bestseller, detailing his journey building The Estée Lauder Cos. Inc. into a global empire. He emphasizes the importance of hiring smart people, maintaining an optimistic and fearless attitude, and continuously striving for improvement, as exemplified by key strategic decisions like launching Clinique and expanding into the U.K. during his tenure. Lauder shares insights into leadership, decision-making, and his belief that anyone can achieve success with courage and effort.

title: Global Over the Top Market - Featuring 8*8 Inc., Alphabet Inc., and Amazon.com Inc. Among Others | Technavio
summary: The global Over the Top (OTT) market is projected to grow by USD 88.85 billion during 2020-2024, at a CAGR of almost 14%. This growth is primarily driven by the increasing demand for cloud streaming services and the rising adoption of target advertisement-based streaming applications. Technavio's report provides a comprehensive analysis including market sizing, forecast, trends, growth drivers, challenges, and vendor analysis featuring key players like 8x8 Inc., Alphabet Inc., Amazon.com Inc., and Netflix Inc.

title: Amazon takes on India giant Reliance in court fight over retailer
summary: Amazon and Reliance Industries are battling in court over the acquisition of Indian retailer Future Group, sparking a "foreign versus local" debate in India's trillion-dollar consumer market. Amazon alleges Future Group violated a contract by agreeing to sell its assets to Reliance, while Reliance and Future Group argue Amazon's actions are detrimental to a local company and that the deal is crucial for Future's survival. The outcome will significantly impact the future of e-commerce and foreign investment in India.

title: Vanke Sues US Partner Over Struggling NYC Project and More Asia Real Estate Headlines
summary: Chinese developer Vanke is suing its US partner RFR Holding over their luxury residential project in Midtown Manhattan, accusing RFR of conflict of interest. Meanwhile, JD.com's logistics unit is reportedly planning an IPO targeting a $40 billion valuation, and Amazon is in court in India over a retail battle with Reliance Industries Ltd. The article also covers other real estate news including Cromwell E-REIT acquiring an Italian logistics park and China Resources Land's services unit launching an IPO.

title: A|I: The AI Times – The AI that fails to see women at all
summary: This article compiles the latest news in AI, machine learning, big data, and automation. Key topics include DarwinAI's partnership with Red Hat to deploy a COVID-19 solution, research from the University of Alberta on using machine learning to fill in public health data, and Rockwell Automation's acquisition of Toronto-based Fiix Inc. A central concern highlighted is the bias in AI image recognition that misinterprets women, along with Roche's new AI and digital health initiative, Autodesk's acquisition of Spacemaker, and the LAPD's ban on commercial facial recognition.

title: Hisense 65-Inch 4K TV At $250 Headlines Budget Smart TV Deals For Black Friday
summary: This article highlights budget-friendly 4K Smart TV deals available for Black Friday, emphasizing large screen sizes under $500. It features various TVs from brands like Insignia, Samsung, TCL, Hisense, and Toshiba, with screen sizes ranging from 32 to 70 inches and different smart TV platforms. The author suggests these deals are suitable for most users looking for good value without premium prices.

title: FedEx, UPS Feel Van Squeeze Amid E-Commerce Rush
summary: FedEx and UPS are experiencing a shortage of delivery vans, leading to unexpected costs and impacting profits during a surge in e-commerce. The scarcity is due to pandemic-induced factory shutdowns and increased demand for home deliveries, forcing couriers to rent vehicles and even purchase used vans. Despite these challenges, the companies do not expect the shortage to hinder delivery capacity, but it adds to the rising expense of doing business.

title: Expanded Pure-as-a-Service Launched
summary: Pure Storage has updated its Pure-as-a-Service solution, transitioning towards a consumption model for storage services on-prem, in the cloud, or via a hybrid model, distinguishing itself from traditional leasing arrangements. A significant change is the publishing of MSRP for the consumption model, including a new service catalog and lower entry points for various block storage and Ultra-Fast File and Object (UFFO) offerings. The article also highlights areas for future improvement, such as clearer performance metrics and a discussion on system upgrades over time to align more with a cloud-like consumption experience.

title: NHN, Intel team up to take on cloud business
summary: South Korean IT company NHN Corp. and Intel Corp. have formed a strategic partnership to expand their presence in the cloud market. This collaboration includes product development like NHN's new DaaS powered by Intel Optane, the launch of the AI-driven Toast Cloud Center 2, and a focus on global market expansion. The move comes as cloud computing services are experiencing significant growth, with many tech giants investing in data centers in Korea.

title: FedEx, UPS see delivery van shortage amid e-commerce rush
summary: FedEx and UPS are reportedly facing a shortage of delivery vans due to the surge in e-commerce. This issue is highlighted in an article by Thomas Black from Bloomberg, published in Automotive News. The increased demand for online shopping has put a strain on the availability of vehicles essential for package delivery.

title: Top-Selling Videogames of the Last 25 Years Show Mario and Call of Duty Rule
summary: A report on the top-selling videogames over the past 25 years reveals the dominance of franchises like Super Mario and Call of Duty. While new games are constantly released, sequels and reboots from major publishers such as Activision Blizzard, Electronic Arts, and Nintendo consistently lead sales charts. The article also highlights the significant growth of mobile gaming revenue and the burgeoning popularity of live-streaming and esports viewership.

title: Alphabet’s (Google’s) first catastrophe bond priced on-target at $237.5m
summary: Alphabet (Google's parent company) has successfully priced its first catastrophe bond, Phoenician Re Ltd. (Series 2020-1), at the target size of $237.5 million. This cat bond will provide Alphabet with California earthquake insurance protection through its captive insurer and Hannover Re, marking a significant step for a major tech company entering the catastrophe bond market for efficient risk transfer. The bond offers a 3% coupon to investors across a three-year term.

title: Amazon's hiring spree of hundreds of thousands of workers gets its real test starting Black Friday
summary: Amazon's extensive hiring spree and logistics investments are being put to the test this Black Friday and holiday season amidst unprecedented online demand due to the pandemic. While the company has significantly ramped up capacity and is considered well-prepared, the true challenge may arise mid-December when shipping carriers enforce delivery deadlines, potentially driving a massive influx of last-minute shoppers to Amazon's robust in-house network. Amazon is also implementing subtle strategies like promoting "no-rush shipping" and alternative delivery options to manage the increased volume.

title: Zoom has picked Amazon Web Services as its preferred cloud provider, months after forming a partnership with Oracle
summary: Zoom has chosen Amazon Web Services (AWS) as its preferred cloud provider, despite having formed a significant partnership with Oracle months earlier to handle increased traffic during the pandemic. This new multi-year agreement strengthens Zoom's long-standing relationship with AWS, integrating new AI features into its Zoom Rooms product via Alexa for Business. While Zoom continues to use other cloud services like Oracle and Microsoft Azure, designating AWS as preferred signals a deeper commitment, driven by AWS's scalability in handling Zoom's massive growth during the pandemic.

title: Amazon.com facilities at Cecil, St. Johns take steps
summary: Amazon.com is moving forward with the development of two new facilities in Jacksonville, Florida. One is a 278,237-square-foot building in AllianceFlorida at Cecil Commerce Center, coded JAX9, with a construction cost of $40.4 million. The other is a 125,000-square-foot last-mile delivery station, DJX6, in St. Johns County near St. Augustine Outlets.

title: Hudson Pacific, partner flex in Seattle with $625M acquisition of Amazon-leased tower
summary: Hudson Pacific Properties and Canada Pension Plan Investment Board have acquired Amazon's Blackfoot building in Seattle for $625 million. This acquisition includes a 10-year lease renewal by Amazon for the 36-story tower.
